label: early copy-phase input n (recall 1-2)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.02% of steps). About 78% of activation mass is in the copy phase, and 71% falls on recall_idx 1-2, i.e. the second and third copy steps. The input token is mostly n (69% of mass, 22x lift), then f (13%). The strongest examples are n fed back when orig(0)=n (just after <DEL>) or when orig(1)=n after o or v (o n, v n). A smaller share, about 22% of mass, is in the original phase at t=3-5 on tokens like 3, l, z or n. Within the predicted condition, magnitude is only weakly modulated: activations are higher for shorter L (3-5) and when the next tokens to output are digits, but neither condition sharpens precision much. The feature does not fire at t<3, on the delimiter, or late in the copy phase (recall_idx >= 3). It also stays silent on most early-copy n inputs: precision is only about 3%, so the deciding context is not captured by simple token or position variables.
